title: CID: Measuring Feature Importance Through Counterfactual Distributions
abstract: arXiv:2511.15371v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Assessing the importance of individual features in Machine Learning is critical to understand the model's decision-making process. While numerous methods exist, the lack of a definitive ground truth for comparison highlights the need for alternative, well-founded measures. This paper introduces a novel post-hoc local feature importance method called Counterfactual Importance Distribution (CID). We generate two sets of positive and negative counterfactuals, model their distributions using Kernel Density Estimation, and rank features based on a distributional dissimilarity measure. This measure, grounded in a rigorous mathematical framework, satisfies key properties required to function as a valid metric. We showcase the effectiveness of our method by comparing with well-established local feature importance explainers. Our method not only offers complementary perspectives to existing approaches, but also improves performance on faithfu

translated_title: CID：通过反事实分布测量特征重要性
translated_abstract: 评估机器学习中各个特征的重要性对于理解模型的决策过程至关重要。尽管目前已存在众多方法，但由于缺乏确凿的基准真值用于比较，凸显了对其他具有坚实理论基础的方法的需求。本文提出了一种新颖的事后局部特征重要性方法，称为反事实重要性分布（CID）。我们生成两组正反事实和负反事实样本，使用核密度估计对其分布进行建模，并基于一种分布差异性度量对特征进行排序。该度量建立在严格的数学框架之上，满足作为有效度量所要求的关键性质。我们通过与成熟的局部特征重要性解释方法进行比较，展示了本方法的有效性。我们的方法不仅为现有方法提供了互补的视角，还在忠实性方面提升了性能。
tldr: 提出了一种名为CID的事后局部特征重要性方法，通过核密度估计建模正负反事实的分布并基于严格的数学框架以分布差异性度量对特征排序，为现有解释方法提供了互补视角并提升了忠实性。
en_tdlr: Proposes CID, a novel post-hoc local feature importance method that models the distributions of positive and negative counterfactuals via kernel density estimation and ranks features using a mathematically grounded distributional dissimilarity measure, offering complementary perspectives to existing explainers and improving faithfulness.
